clause: Hilbert-self-adjoint generator, bounded port, nonreal resolvent
draft_quote: Throughout this section $\mathcal X$ is a complex Hilbert space
evidence_or_owed: The opening fixes a self-adjoint H in a Hilbert space, a bounded port from a port space of any dimension, and the nonreal resolvent. Section 1 states the same hypotheses on the output space.

clause: Compressed resolvent of a bounded port
evidence_or_owed: The displayed equation defines the response on the complement of the real axis for a port space of any dimension.

clause: Scope of the definition: interior, finite-rank and regularized singular inputs (following discussion)
draft_quote: It covers a port inside the system, a port of finite rank, and a singular input
evidence_or_owed: TAUM's sentence after the definition is carried in the opening.

clause: Holomorphy off the real axis and adjoint symmetry
evidence_or_owed: Stated and proved from norm analyticity and the adjoint symmetry of the resolvent.

clause: Positive imaginary part and its exact factorization on the upper half-plane
evidence_or_owed: The proof compresses the one-point resolvent identity and exhibits the imaginary part as a positive operator.

clause: Two-point Nevanlinna kernel
evidence_or_owed: Defined on pairs of points of the upper half-plane.

clause: Two-point resolvent factorization and positive kernel
evidence_or_owed: The two-point resolvent identity gives the factorization. The quadratic sum is displayed as a squared norm for every finite choice of points and port vectors.

clause: Positive self-adjoint return on the input sector
evidence_or_owed: Part (a) uses the positive self-adjoint return stated after the cohomology formula of Section 7.

clause: Canonical compressed resolvent for the A*A choice
evidence_or_owed: The canonical response is displayed for every bounded input into the physical space.

clause: Herglotz and positive-kernel conclusions for this choice
evidence_or_owed: Part (a) applies both propositions with H equal to the return.

clause: Port identity on the retained sector
evidence_or_owed: Part (b) compresses the Schur formula of Section 8 by a port that maps into the retained space.

clause: Passive response of the full Hilbert block
evidence_or_owed: The block operator is self-adjoint as a bounded symmetric perturbation of the direct sum of its diagonal blocks, so its response through the embedded port satisfies both propositions.

clause: Limit of positivity for the Krein branch
draft_quote: No such positivity is assumed here.
evidence_or_owed: Established by a witness: a two-by-two generator self-adjoint for the indefinite form, with real eigenvalues 1 and 2, whose response through the first coordinate has imaginary part -6/5 at z = 2 + i/2. Which further assumptions restore positivity is a separate question and is not part of this clause.

clause: Operator Cayley transform of the passive response
evidence_or_owed: Defined on the upper half-plane.

clause: Bounded invertibility of the Cayley denominator
evidence_or_owed: First statement of the proposition, with the lower bounds for the operator and its adjoint, closed dense range, and an inverse of norm at most one for port spaces of any dimension.

clause: Analyticity, defect identity and contractivity
evidence_or_owed: The congruence with four times the imaginary part is derived and the norm bound follows.

clause: Operator-valued de Branges–Rovnyak kernel
evidence_or_owed: Defined with the denominator and sign convention of TAUM.

clause: Kernel factorization, positivity and reproducing space
evidence_or_owed: The factorization with the two Cayley factors and the factor two is proved, and positivity follows by congruence. The reproducing-kernel consequence is stated with a citation and is not reproved.

clause: Positive operator weights at the response lines
evidence_or_owed: The paragraph after the definition identifies the atoms of the measure with the weights of Corollary 1.3.

clause: Borel measure and total mass for arbitrary spectra
evidence_or_owed: Defined on all Borel sets with total mass, weak countable additivity, and the scalar complex measures used for integration.

clause: Finite-line resolvent and Fourier sums
evidence_or_owed: Both finite sums are displayed after the proposition, for weights of any rank.

clause: General resolvent and time-domain representations
evidence_or_owed: Both operator-valued integrals are stated for an arbitrary compressed spectral measure, with the factor of Planck's constant used in the draft.

clause: Time-domain positive definiteness
evidence_or_owed: The quadratic sum is displayed as the squared norm of a sum of evolved port vectors.

clause: Closed span generated from the port in time
evidence_or_owed: Section 1 defines the space by the time span. The proposition restates it for a port.

clause: Nonreal resolvent-span definition, equivalence, and minimality terminology
evidence_or_owed: The proposition proves that the resolvent span and the time span coincide for arbitrary spectra, by the Laplace representation of the resolvent in one direction and invariance under all resolvents in the other. The sentence after it defines a minimal pair.

clause: Contains the direct range and is invariant under the entire unitary group
evidence_or_owed: Stated in the proposition and proved from the strong limit of the scaled resolvent.

clause: Reducing self-adjoint restriction and exact response invariance
evidence_or_owed: The restriction is self-adjoint, the two responses agree at every nonreal point, and the restricted pair is minimal.

clause: Unique unitary intertwining generators and ports for equal responses
evidence_or_owed: Full proof: equal Gram matrices of resolvent-port vectors, extension by minimality, intertwining of resolvents and hence of generators with their domains, recovery of the ports, and uniqueness. Two continuity steps are written out: the conjugate pair of points in the Gram formula, which TAUM mentions, and equal points in the resolvent identity, which it does not.

clause: Rank count for the indirect space and decomposition of the full defect
evidence_or_owed: Unchanged. Section 1 states and proves the count and the decomposition of the adjoint kernel. The fragment repeats the hypothesis of finite-rank weights where it uses the count.

clause: Port-coordinate invariance and the rank condition for injectivity (following discussion)
draft_quote: an invertible change of coordinates $T$ on $\mathcal E$ preserves it
evidence_or_owed: The first remark gives invariance under a change of port coordinates. The last sentences give the kernel condition for an injective port.

clause: Relations between the weight ranges (following discussion)
draft_quote: The count is the dimension of the space of relations
evidence_or_owed: The second remark proves that the range of the summed weight is the sum of the ranges, identifies the count with the dimension of the space of relations, and gives the direct-sum criterion for a zero count.

clause: Enlarging the port can change the count (following discussion)
draft_quote: Third, enlarging the port can change the count.
evidence_or_owed: TAUM asserts this without an example. The fragment gives one from the pair model: an interior preparation has count one, and adding the endpoint preparation makes it zero. The check also gives a case where the count rises.

clause: Invisible complement and observability of indirect directions
evidence_or_owed: Unchanged. Proposition 1.1 identifies the permanently invisible vectors with the orthogonal complement of the reached space.

clause: Scope of the invisibility statement: one port and all real times (following discussion)
draft_quote: These statements concern one port and all real times.
evidence_or_owed: TAUM's caution about finite observation windows and other observables is restated, with a pointer to the semibounded waiting proposition and the translation example of Section 1.

clause: Orbital realization with and without the filter
draft_quote: The trap of Section~\ref{subsec:orbital-apparatus} is the instance
evidence_or_owed: Section 8 works the trap out. The fragment names it as the instance of the general proposition, with and without the filter.

clause: General matched-measure factorization and departure
evidence_or_owed: Stated for strongly commuting H0 and L and equal scalar measures in opposite charge sectors: the orthonormal triple, the isometric port, the cosine factor, the weight on the indirect space and the time of complete departure.

clause: Fixed analysis line and weight outside the three-dimensional carrier
draft_quote: If the two shifted spectral branches overlap
evidence_or_owed: The amplitude on the fixed line and the weight outside the three vectors are in the proposition. The caveat that the line need not lie in the reached space is kept, with an explicit overlapping example that TAUM does not give.

clause: Matched measures from a unitary reflection or time reversal (following discussion)
draft_quote: follow from a unitary reflection, or from an antiunitary symmetry such as time reversal
evidence_or_owed: Carried with the reason the antiunitary case still gives equal measures.

clause: Ground needs a no-crossing condition; complete departure without complete return (following discussion)
draft_quote: Three limits of the proposition should be kept.
evidence_or_owed: Both cautions are carried: Lg = 0 keeps g an eigenvector only, and the return weight at the stated times is the squared zero-field amplitude.

clause: Bounded trace between a Hamiltonian Hilbert scale and a port space
draft_quote: A \emph{distributional trace} is a bounded operator
evidence_or_owed: The scale, its anti-dual with the carrier as pivot, the bounded trace and its adjoint are defined before the proposition.

clause: Bounded smoothed port, Herglotz response and finite spectral mass
evidence_or_owed: The port is defined as the adjoint of a bounded operator on the carrier, which gives TAUM's formula without separately extending the Gaussian to the negative scale. The statement names the eight propositions that apply to a bounded port. The paragraph after it says that the finite count and the sector proposition keep their own hypotheses.

clause: Complete eigenbasis and formal port coefficients for heat smoothing
draft_quote: Suppose $H$ has a complete orthonormal basis of eigenvectors
evidence_or_owed: The eigenbasis, real eigenvalues and coefficient vectors in the port space are specified with no assumption of finite spectral support.

clause: Weighted summability, Hilbert–Schmidt port, response series and mass
evidence_or_owed: The port, its Hilbert-Schmidt norm, the response series with locally uniform norm convergence and the total mass with trace-norm convergence are stated and proved.

clause: Support normalization of a bounded port by its polar part
draft_quote: is the port normalized on its support
evidence_or_owed: The polar part restricted to the support is identified as the normalized port and tied to the polar port of Section 1.

clause: Application to heat-smoothed scalar and operator-valued ports
draft_quote: A smoothed port has no preferred scale.
evidence_or_owed: The scalar normalization to unit mass and the operator-valued case are given, including a mass spectrum that accumulates at zero.
